claim: Newts have the ability to repeatedly regenerate their lens even during ageing.
source: Newts have the ability to repeatedly regenerate their lens even during ageing.
evidence: This is a primary assertion of the study supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Repeatedly regenerated lenses showed a robust transcriptional program comparable to young never-regenerated lenses.
source: Our analysis indicates that repeatedly regenerated lenses showed a robust transcriptional program comparable to young never-regenerated lenses.
evidence: Supported by transcriptomic analysis comparing #19 and #0 lens samples showing no significant differential gene expression.

claim: The tail, which was never regenerated, showed gene expression signatures of ageing.
source: In contrast, the tail, which was never regenerated, showed gene expression signatures of ageing.
evidence: Supported by differential gene expression analysis showing 4204 genes with FDR<0.05 and FC>2 in tail samples.

claim: Newts appear to regenerate using cells recruited locally from the site of the insult.
source: Importantly, newts appear to regenerate using cells recruited locally from the site of the insult.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about newt regeneration.

claim: During limb regeneration, cells at the site of amputation dedifferentiate and then redifferentiate to reconstruct the lost part.
source: For example, during limb regeneration, the cells at the site of amputation, such as muscle and bone cells, dedifferentiate and then redifferentiate to reconstruct the lost part (Tsonis, 1996; Sandoval-Guzmán et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Lens regeneration is possible following complete removal of the lens.
source: First, regeneration is possible following complete removal of the lens, and thus whole-organ regeneration occurs.
evidence: This is stated as an established characteristic of newt lens regeneration.

claim: The lens is regenerated from pigment epithelial cells of the dorsal iris via transdifferentiation.
source: Second, the lens is regenerated from a different tissue, that is, the pigment epithelial cells (PECs) of the dorsal iris, via transdifferentiation rather than from the remaining lens tissue (Henry and Tsonis, 2010; Barbosa-Sabanero et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Lenses were removed from the same animals 18 times over a 16-year period.
source: During this period, lenses were removed from the same animals 18 times.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The 17 and 18 times regenerated lenses were virtually identical to intact lenses from 14-year-old newts that had never undergone lentectomy.
source: Previously, it was shown that the 17 and 18 times regenerated lenses, which were obtained from the second-to-last and last collections, respectively, were virtually identical to the intact lenses removed from full-grown, 14-year-old newts produced from fertilized eggs that had never undergone a lentectomy or lens regeneration.
evidence: This refers to previously published findings.

claim: No significant delay in the lens regeneration process was observed in any of the 18 repetitions over 16 years.
source: Throughout this 16-year period, the rate and stage of regeneration was carefully evaluated, and no significant delay in the lens regeneration process was observed in any of the 18 repetitions (Eguchi et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The experimental and control lenses were of the same size and transparency at the gross anatomical level.
source: At the gross anatomical level, the experimental and control lenses were of the same size and transparency.
evidence: This is an observational finding from the study.

claim: The lens fiber organization appeared normal, with the nucleus containing primary fibers and the cortex containing secondary fibers.
source: The lens fiber organization appeared normal, with the nucleus containing primary fibers and the cortex containing secondary fibers.
evidence: This is an observational finding from the study.

claim: The gene expression patterns of the experimental and control lenses were very similar.
source: Most importantly, the gene expression patterns of the experimental and control lenses were very similar.
evidence: This is supported by the transcriptomic analysis presented in the study.

claim: The age of the animal does not affect its regenerative capacity.
source: The study also established that the age of the animal does not affect its regenerative capacity (see also Sousounis et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research and the current study's findings.

claim: The newts were estimated to be at least 14 years old at the onset of the project and at least 30 years old at the end.
source: The newts were estimated to be at least 14 years old at the onset of the project and thus would have been at least 30 years old at the end of the study.
evidence: This describes the age of the experimental animals.

claim: The reported lifespan of the Japanese newt is 25 years.
source: Because the reported lifespan of the Japanese newt is 25 years (Goin et al., 1978), this group truly represents an old population.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The experimental group comprised 32-year-old newts whose lenses had been removed 19 times.
source: The experimental group (referred to as #19 throughout) comprised of 32-year-old newts whose lenses had been removed 19 times.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The control group consisted of 14-year-old newts that had their original lenses.
source: The control group (referred to as #0) consisted of 14-year-old newts that had their original lenses (i.e., non-regenerated lenses) (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and is illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Nearly 4.5 billion reads were generated with approximately 150 million reads per sample.
source: We generated nearly 4.5 billion reads, with approximately 150 million reads per sample.
evidence: This describes the sequencing output of the study.

claim: More than 97% of reads passed TAILING:30 criteria using Trimmomatic.
source: The reads were of high quality (>97% passed TAILING:30 criteria using Trimmomatic [Bolger et al., 2014])
evidence: This describes the quality control results of the sequencing data.

claim: Approximately 2% of reads were duplicates as assessed using FastUniq.
source: and included very few duplicates (approximately 2%, as assessed using FastUniq [Xu et al., 2012]).
evidence: This describes the quality control results of the sequencing data.

claim: The reference transcriptome was composed of 4.3 million contigs and isoforms.
source: Trinity was used for de novo assembly of the reference transcriptome (see Materials and methods), which was composed of 4.3 million contigs and isoforms (referred to as transcripts or genes throughout).
evidence: This describes the assembly results.

claim: 133,503 transcripts (73,233 contigs) were annotated against the human reference proteome.
source: We used NCBI BLASTx to annotate 133,503 (73,233 contigs) of the transcripts against the human reference proteome obtained from UniProt (e-value<1E-10).
evidence: This describes the annotation results.

claim: 58,331 of the annotated transcripts were related to human transposons (43.7%).
source: Remarkably, 58,331 of these transcripts were related to human transposons (43.7%).
evidence: This describes the annotation results.

claim: 15,077 non-redundant annotations were obtained representing nearly 75% of all human genes.
source: In total, we obtained 15,077 non-redundant annotations representing nearly 75% of all human genes.
evidence: This describes the annotation results.

claim: Alpha-, beta-, and gamma-crystallin genes were the highest expressed genes in lens samples.
source: As expected alpha-, beta-, and gamma-crystallin genes (CRY) were found to be the highest expressed genes in lens samples.
evidence: This is supported by the expression analysis presented in the study.

claim: Crystallins are the major structural protein of the lens.
source: Crystallins are known to be the major structural protein of the lens (Masters et al., 1977).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The lens dataset contained lens fiber major intrinsic protein MIP and phakinin (BFSP2), genes highly expressed in lenses.
source: The same dataset also contained the lens fiber major intrinsic protein MIP, and phakinin (BFSP2), genes highly expressed in lenses (Figure 2B; orange) (Broekhuyse and Kuhlmann, 1974; Maisel and Perry, 1972).
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2B and citations to previous research.

claim: Ornithine decarboxylase antizyme 1 (OAZ1), hemoglobin subunit alpha (HBA1), and cell division control protein 42 homolog (CDC42) were the highest expressed genes in iris samples.
source: Ornithine decarboxylase antizyme 1 (OAZ1), hemoglobin subunit alpha (HBA1), and cell division control protein 42 homolog (CDC42) were the highest expressed genes in the iris samples (Figure 2B; red).
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Keratin (KRT) and ribosomal protein genes were the ones with the highest expression in tails.
source: Expectedly, keratin (KRT) and ribosomal protein genes were the ones with the highest expression in tails (Figure 2B; yellow).
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Keratin proteins are known to be expressed in the skin.
source: Keratin proteins are known to be expressed in the skin.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Six genes (five coding for ribosomal proteins and one for ferritin heavy chain) were the most expressed in all tissue types.
source: Six genes, five coding for ribosomal proteins and one for the ferritin heavy chain, were found to be the most expressed in all tissue types (Figure 2B; purple).
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Lens preferentially expressed crystallins, lens fiber membrane intrinsic protein LIM2, filensin (BFSP1), and tudor domain-containing protein 7 (TDRD7).
source: Genes in the lens dataset included crystallins, lens fiber membrane intrinsic protein LIM2, filensin (BFSP1), and tudor domain-containing protein 7 (TDRD7), among others (Figure 2C; orange).
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: LIM2, BFSP1, and TDRD7 are known to be expressed in lenses.
source: LIM2, BFSP1, and TDRD7 are known to be expressed in lenses (Church and Wang, 1993; Hess et al., 1998; Lachke et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Iris preferentially expressed retinal pigment epithelial (RPE)-retinal G protein-coupled receptor (RGR).
source: Iris preferentially expressed retinal pigment epithelial (RPE)-retinal G protein-coupled receptor (RGR), a protein found in pigmented cells of the retina (Figure 2C; red) (Tao et al., 1998)
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2C and citation to previous research.

claim: Tail samples expressed keratins, creatine kinase M-type (CKM), resistin (RETN), and alpha skeletal muscle actin (ACTA1).
source: while tail samples expressed keratins, creatine kinase M-type (CKM), resistin (RETN), and alpha skeletal muscle actin (ACTA1) (Figure 2C; yellow), proteins found in muscle, skin, and adipose tissue (Way et al., 2001; Nowak et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by expression data shown in Figure 2C and citations to previous research.

claim: No genes were found to differ significantly in their expression between the #19 and #0 lens samples (FDR<0.05 and FC>2).
source: No genes were found to differ significantly in their expression between the #19 and #0 lens samples (false discovery rate [FDR] <0.05 and fold change [FC] >2; Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a key finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: In iris samples, 311 genes (54 annotated) were found with FDR<0.05 and FC>2.
source: In the iris samples, we found 311 (54 of these annotated) genes with FDR<0.05 and FC>2 (Figure 3A and Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In tail samples, 4204 genes (780 annotated) were found with FDR<0.05 and FC>2.
source: We found 4204 (780 of these annotated) genes with FDR<0.05 and FC >2 (Figure 3B and Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: GO terms related to translation, electron transport chain, oxidation reduction, and mitochondrion were enriched in the group of down-regulated genes in #19 tail samples.
source: Enrichment analysis revealed that GO terms related to translation, electron transport chain, oxidation reduction, and mitochondrion were enriched in the group of down-regulated genes in the #19 tail samples (Figure 3C; green bars; FDR<0.05, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Iris samples showed enrichment of electron transport chain genes in the down-regulation dataset.
source: As will be discussed later, iris samples also showed enrichment of electron transport chain genes in the down-regulation dataset.
evidence: This is stated as a finding that will be discussed later in the manuscript.

claim: Down-regulation of electron transport chain-associated genes is a well-established signature of ageing in many vertebrate animal models and flies.
source: Down-regulation of electron transport chain-associated genes is a well-established signature of ageing in many vertebrate animal models and flies (López-Otín et al., 2013; Zahn et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: 16 genes with GO terms related to ageing and/or senescence were differentially regulated between #0 and #19 tail samples.
source: To further illustrate this, we data-mined genes with GO terms related to ageing and/or senescence, which were differentially regulated between #0 and #19 tail samples and found 16 genes (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Iris is the most complex tissue followed by the tail and the lens based on transcriptomic complexity.
source: This analysis reveals that iris is the most complex tissue followed by the tail and the lens (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic complexity analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: #19 iris and tail samples showed slightly increased complexity versus the respective #0 samples.
source: Interestingly, #19 iris and tail samples showed slightly increased complexity versus the respective #0 samples.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic complexity analysis.

claim: #19 lens samples showed the lowest increase in transcriptomic complexity.
source: #19 lens samples showed the lowest increase corroborating our previous data indicating no significant changes between #0 and #19 lens samples maintaining a stable gene expression profile.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic complexity analysis.

claim: When genes from #19 lenses were compared with those from #0 lenses, a nearly uniform pattern was obtained across all 10 samples.
source: When the genes from the #19 lenses (EL1–EL5) were compared with those from the #0 lenses (CL1–CL5), a nearly uniform pattern was obtained across all 10 samples.
evidence: This is a finding from the sample correlation analysis.

claim: The experimental and control lens samples did not segregate via cladograms, indicating high correlation for overall gene expression pattern.
source: This pattern similarity was also evidenced by the lack of segregation of the experimental and control lens samples via cladograms. These results indicate that these samples were highly correlated for their overall gene expression pattern.
evidence: This is a finding from the sample correlation analysis.

claim: Irises and tails showed a characteristic four-boxed color pattern on the sample correlation matrix plot indicating differences in overall correlation between #19 and #0 samples.
source: However, a different pattern emerged when comparing the irises and tails between the #19 and #0 groups. Areas on the sample correlation matrix plot showed the characteristic four-boxed color pattern indicating differences in the overall correlation between #19 and #0 samples (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the sample correlation analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The five biological replicates of each tissue had high correlation values among them.
source: By dissecting the within tissue correlation values and comparing them, it was evident that the five biological replicates of each tissue had high correlation values among them (Figure 4B; solid colors and big-dotted bars).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: When comparisons are made between #0 and #19 samples, the correlation drops with lens samples showing the least decrease compared to iris and tail.
source: However, when comparisons are made between #0 and #19 samples (Figure 4B; small-dotted bars), the correlation drops with lens samples showing the least decrease (orange bars) compared to iris (red bars) and tail (yellow bars).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Iris and lens tissues were the most related while lens and tail tissues were the least related based on genes expressed.
source: We also performed a comparison between tissues and found that iris and lens tissues were the most related while lens and tail tissues the least related based on the genes expressed (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the between-tissue correlation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Sample EL4 did not strongly correlate with the other lens samples.
source: Sample correlation matrix plot also revealed that sample EL4 (one from #19 old newts) did not strongly correlate with the other lens samples.
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis.

claim: The correlation values of EL4 sample were the lowest for the within tissue comparisons performed.
source: The correlation values of this sample were the lowest for the within tissue comparisons performed (Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This is a finding from the correlation analysis.

claim: 30% of the transcripts associated with crystallin genes were deregulated in the EL4 sample.
source: Our analysis revealed that 30% of the transcripts associated with crystallin genes were deregulated in the EL4 sample.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of the EL4 sample.

claim: Most deregulated crystallin genes in EL4 showed higher expression than other #19 lens samples, which does not match a pathological profile.
source: However, most of them showed higher expression in the EL4 sample than the other #19 lens samples, an expression pattern that does not match a pathological profile.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the expression data from the EL4 sample analysis.

claim: Transcript c1474631_g1 corresponding to gamma crystallin B showed more than twofold up-regulation in EL4.
source: For example, transcript c1474631_g1 corresponding to gamma crystallin B, a highly expressed gene in the lens, showed a more than twofold up-regulation (Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is a specific finding from the EL4 sample analysis.

claim: EL4 had the weakest association among the #19 lens samples and #0 young control lenses, but differences in gene expression were not strongly associated with ageing or disease.
source: Overall, our analysis showed that EL4 had the weakest association among the #19 lens samples and #0 young control lenses; however, differences in gene expression were not strongly associated with ageing or disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the EL4 sample analysis.

claim: 311 genes were differentially affected when #0 and #19 iris samples were compared.
source: As mentioned earlier, 311 genes were found to be differentially affected when #0 and #19 iris samples were compared (Figure 3A, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: The age-regulated profile of the iris was corrected during the lens regeneration process.
source: Surprisingly though, the lens samples did not have any significantly deregulated genes suggesting that the age-regulated profile of the iris was corrected during the regeneration process.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the differential expression findings.

claim: Lens FPKM values were highly correlated (r = 0.9982) and differed on average 27% (slope m = 0.7293).
source: As expected lens FPKM values were highly correlated (r = 0.9982) and differed between them on average 27% (slope; m = 0.7293) (Figure 5A; orange).
evidence: This is a finding from the linear regression analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Iris FPKM values were not correlated (r = 0.0070) and differed completely (m = 0.004).
source: On the other hand, iris FPKM values were not correlated and differed completely (r = 0.0070, m = 0.004, Figure 5A; red).
evidence: This is a finding from the linear regression analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Deregulation of genes in the iris were corrected in the regenerated lens.
source: These data clearly indicate that deregulation of these genes were corrected in the regenerated lens.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the linear regression analysis.

claim: Electron transport chain was enriched in the group of genes that were down-regulated in #19 iris samples.
source: When the function of the annotated genes was investigated, we found that electron transport chain was enriched in the group of genes that were down-regulated in the #19 iris samples (Figure 5B; green bars, Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This is a finding from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: #19 repetitive regenerated lenses did not inherit the down-regulation of electron transport chain genes during transdifferentiation.
source: As indicated above, this is a well-established ageing signature and suggests that #19 repetitive regenerated lenses did not inherit it during the transdifferentiation process.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the GO enrichment findings and established knowledge about ageing.

claim: Repeated lens regeneration employs a robust transcriptomic program that is maintained throughout life.
source: Overall, our results point out that repeated lens regeneration employs a robust transcriptomic program that is maintained throughout life, an attribute not found in the never-regenerated tail tissue from the same animals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Repeated regeneration might ameliorate age-regulated gene changes.
source: In addition, the fact that #19 lenses did not show down-regulation of genes related to electron transport chain, a well-established signature of ageing revealed in #19 iris and tail samples, suggests that repeated regeneration might ameliorate age-regulated gene changes.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the findings.

claim: Genes preferentially and highly expressed in lens or tail are known to be expressed in other vertebrates.
source: We found that genes preferentially and highly expressed in lens or tail are known to be expressed in other vertebrates.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the comparative analysis.

claim: Crystallins, phakinin, filensin, tudor domain-containing protein 7, lens fiber major intrinsic protein MIP, and lens fiber membrane intrinsic protein LIM2 are major structural/molecular components of the lens.
source: More importantly for the lens, crystallins, phakinin, filensin, tudor domain-containing protein 7, lens fiber major intrinsic protein MIP, and lens fiber membrane intrinsic protein LIM2 are major structural/molecular components of the lens and linked to age-related lens diseases when deregulated (Sousounis et al., 2014; Lachke et al., 2011; Sousounis and Tsonis, 2012; Jakobs et al., 2000; Ramachandran et al., 2007; Berry et al., 2000; Pras et al., 2002 ).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: These lens genes are linked to age-related lens diseases when deregulated.
source: More importantly for the lens, crystallins, phakinin, filensin, tudor domain-containing protein 7, lens fiber major intrinsic protein MIP, and lens fiber membrane intrinsic protein LIM2 are major structural/molecular components of the lens and linked to age-related lens diseases when deregulated (Sousounis et al., 2014; Lachke et al., 2011; Sousounis and Tsonis, 2012; Jakobs et al., 2000; Ramachandran et al., 2007; Berry et al., 2000; Pras et al., 2002 ).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The #19 lenses showed no differences in size, transparency, or overall fiber structure compared to non-regenerated lenses from younger animals.
source: In addition, compared with the non-regenerated lenses from younger animals, the #19 lenses showed no differences in size, transparency, or overall fiber structure (Figure 6)
evidence: This is an observational finding illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: During the 18-year experiment, cataracts were never observed in the regenerated lenses.
source: and during this 18-year experiment, cataracts were never observed in the regenerated lenses.
evidence: This is an observational finding from the long-term study.

claim: Repeated lentectomies and ageing have no effect on lens regeneration, development, or homeostasis.
source: This important result clearly demonstrates that repeated lentectomies and ageing have no effect on lens regeneration, development, or homeostasis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: Lenses are severely affected by ageing with marked changes in expression of mitochondrion electron transport chain, oxidative stress and crystallin genes.
source: In addition to the aforementioned genetic causes of cataracts, it is well documented that lenses are severely affected by ageing with marked changes in expression of mitochondrion electron transport chain, oxidative stress and crystallin genes as well as alterations of the fiber structure and homeostasis leading to cataracts (Su et al., 2015; Tsentalovich et al., 2015; Wei et al., 2015; Linetsky et al., 2014; Petrash et al., 2013; Sousounis and Tsonis, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The newt #19 lenses show a robust transcriptional program as they undergo multiple events of regeneration throughout their lives.
source: Based on these observations, the newt #19 lenses show a robust transcriptional program as they undergo multiple events of regeneration throughout their lives.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: The process of transdifferentiation might provide robustness to the process of regeneration.
source: Conceptually the process of transdifferentiation might provide robustness to the process of regeneration.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation.

claim: The transdifferentiation ability of even aged human iris PECs is retained in vitro.
source: In relation to this, it is interesting to note that the transdifferentiation ability of even aged human iris PECs is retained in vitro.
evidence: This is stated as an interesting related finding.

claim: A cell line from an 80-year-old human is capable of transdifferentiating into lens.
source: Previous studies have shown that such a cell line from an 80-year-old human is capable of transdifferentiating into lens (Yun et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Thousands of genes were significantly differentially regulated in #19 versus #0 tails.
source: In contrast to the patterns observed in the lenses, a comparison of gene expression between the #19 and #0 tails revealed striking differences. Thousands of genes were significantly differentially regulated.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Genes encoding proteins that are part of the electron transport chain were among the most highly deregulated genes in #19 tail samples.
source: Among the most highly deregulated genes in the #19 tail samples were those encoding proteins that are part of the electron transport chain (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: Down-regulation of electron transport chain gene-sets are part of an established ageing signature in other vertebrates.
source: Down-regulation of these gene-sets are part of an established ageing signature in other vertebrates (López-Otín et al., 2013; Zahn et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Several ageing- and senescence-related genes were found to be deregulated in #19 tail samples.
source: In addition, several ageing- and senescence-related genes were found to be deregulated in these samples.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis.

claim: The tails of the #19 newts show clear hallmarks of ageing.
source: These findings indicate that the tails of the #19 newts show clear hallmarks of ageing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: A robust transcriptional program ensues after an insult to guarantee that regenerative ability in newts will not be thwarted with age.
source: These observations provide in our opinion strong evidence that a robust transcriptional program ensues after an insult to guarantee that the regenerative ability in newts will not be thwarted with age.
evidence: This is an interpretation and conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: The irises showed an intermediate pattern in gene expression differences, especially with respect to the number of deregulated genes.
source: Although the differences in gene expression between the #19 and #0 tails and lenses were pronounced, the irises showed an intermediate pattern, especially with respect to the number of deregulated genes.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression analysis.

claim: #19 iris samples down-regulated electron transport chain genes, a sign of ageing.
source: Similarly to the #19 tails, #19 iris samples down-regulated electron transport chain genes, a sign of ageing.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential expression and GO enrichment analysis.

claim: Ageing of the iris may hinder the lens regeneration process.
source: Iris is the source of lens regeneration and ageing of this tissue may hinder the process.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the role of iris in lens regeneration.

claim: There should be a mechanism that amends or corrects the profile from the source (dorsal iris) to the regenerated tissue (lens).
source: Since #19 lenses are comparable to #0 and that is not the case for the iris, there should be a mechanism that amends or corrects the profile from the source (dorsal iris) to the regenerated tissue (lens).
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential findings between iris and lens.

claim: All genes that were found to differ in the iris were similar in the regenerate lens.
source: All genes that were found to differ in the iris, the source of lens regeneration, were similar in the regenerate, the lens (Figure 5 and Supplementary files 10, 11).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Contig c1229960_g1 corresponding to NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase chain 1 shows low expression in control iris but high expression in experimental iris, while regenerated lenses show low expression similar to controls.
source: For instance, contig c1229960_g1 corresponding to nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH)-ubiquinone oxidoreductase chain 1, shows a low expression in the control iris samples, but it is highly expressed in the experimental iris samples. However, the same newts with iris tissues that showed this expression profile had regenerated lenses with low expression of the gene, similar to that of the control iris and lens rendering the difference non-significant.
evidence: This is a specific example from the analysis.

claim: Not all dorsal iris PECs contribute to the regeneration of the lost lens.
source: The gene expression differences observed in the iris may also be attributed to the fact that not all dorsal iris PECs contribute to the regeneration of the lost lens.
evidence: This is an interpretation to explain the findings.

claim: After lentectomy, regeneration occurs via dedifferentiation of the lower dorsal tip of the iris.
source: After lentectomy regeneration occurs via dedifferentiation of the lower dorsal tip of the iris.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the regeneration process.

claim: Dorsal iris PECs are either replenished, or cells migrate there from other locations in the iris.
source: These dorsal iris PECs are either replenished, or cells migrate there from other locations in the iris.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the cellular mechanism.

claim: Not the whole dorsal iris is eventually transformed into lens cells and cell proliferation continuously provides the dorsal iris with PECs.
source: Regardless, given that repeated lentectomies always trigger lens regeneration, it is clear that not the whole dorsal iris is eventually transformed into lens cells and that cell proliferation continuously provides the dorsal iris with PECs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the repeated regeneration capability.

claim: Some parts of the dorsal iris are regenerated and might employ a transcriptomic program similar to that of young controls.
source: Consequently, some parts of the dorsal iris are regenerated and might employ a transcriptomic program similar to that of young controls.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation.

claim: Other iris cells might not have regenerative ability and eventually age, reflecting the intermediate ageing profile of this tissue.
source: On the other hand, other cells might not have this ability and eventually age, thus reflecting the intermediate ageing profile of this tissue.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation.

claim: The cellular or transcriptomic correction of the ageing profile observed in iris to the regenerated lens should be critical for the integrity of the newly formed organ.
source: Nevertheless, the cellular or transcriptomic correction of the ageing profile observed in iris to the regenerated lens should be critical for the integrity of the newly formed organ (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an interpretation illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: There is significant turnover of senescent cells during newt limb regeneration.
source: Recently it has been shown that there is significant turnover of senescent cells during newt limb regeneration.
evidence: This is stated as a recent finding.

claim: Turnover of senescent cells might explain why newts can regenerate repeatedly their lost structures throughout their lives.
source: This might explain why newts can regenerate repeatedly their lost structures throughout their lives (Yun et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Senescent cells might be removed from the dorsal iris to ensure the correct process of lens regeneration.
source: As such, the possibility exists that senescent cells are removed from the dorsal iris to ensure the correct process of lens regeneration.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the findings about senescent cell turnover.

claim: The patterns of ageing in newts are similar to those of other species, particularly those related to the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
source: Our results suggest that the patterns of ageing in newts are similar to those of other species, particularly those related to the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the findings and comparison with other species.

claim: The molecular pathways related to ageing have been studied extensively in worms, flies and mice.
source: The molecular pathways related to ageing have been studied extensively in other animal models, particularly worms, flies and mice.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Many genes regulated during ageing have been associated with the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
source: Many of the genes that are regulated during ageing have been associated with the mitochondrial electron transport chain (Zahn et al., 2007; Signer and Morrison, 2013; Gomes et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Insulin signaling negatively regulates the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16.
source: Another major regulatory pathway involves insulin signaling, which negatively regulates the FOXO transcription factor DAF-16.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ageing pathways.

claim: DAF-16 regulates metabolism and oxidative stress by promoting antioxidant enzymes.
source: This transcription factor regulates metabolism and oxidative stress by promoting antioxidant enzymes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about DAF-16 function.

claim: Up-regulation of DAF-16 could enhance longevity.
source: The up-regulation of DAF-16 could enhance longevity (Curran et al., 2009; Curran and Ruvkun, 2007; Murphy et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous research.

claim: These ageing mechanisms might also be involved in regeneration in newts.
source: Thus, it is conceivable that these mechanisms might also be involved in regeneration in newts.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation.

claim: The 18-year-long experiments provide data that render the newt an indispensable model for addressing issues of regeneration and ageing.
source: Consequently, our 18-year-long experiments provide data that render the newt an indispensable model for addressing issues of regeneration and ageing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study.

claim: The study establishes the newt as a key model for the study of regeneration in relation to ageing.
source: In addition, our study provides a new paradigm in biology, and establishes the newt as a key model for the study of regeneration in relation to ageing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract.

claim: Newts are among the few vertebrates that possess the remarkable ability to regenerate tissues, organs, and body parts.
source: Newts are among the few vertebrates that possess the remarkable ability to regenerate tissues, organs, and body parts, including limbs, tails and eye tissue (Sanchez Alvarado and Tsonis, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous research.

claim: If the entire limb is removed, no regeneration occurs.
source: For this process to occur, cells from the original organ must remain to provide a source for regeneration; if the entire limb is removed, no regeneration occurs.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about limb regeneration.

claim: The Japanese newt Cynops pyrrhogaster was used in this study.
source: The Japanese newt C. pyrrhogaster was used in this study.
evidence: This describes the experimental model.

claim: These lenses were regenerated 19 times and removed 18 years after the start of the project.
source: These lenses were regenerated 19 times and removed 18 years after the start of the project.
evidence: This describes the experimental timeline.

claim: The dorsal iris was sampled because this tissue gives rise to the regenerated lens, implying that the dorsal iris had also been regenerated/replenished 19 times.
source: The dorsal iris was sampled because this tissue gives rise to the regenerated lens, which implies that the dorsal iris had also been regenerated/replenished 19 times.
evidence: This explains the rationale for sampling the dorsal iris.

claim: The tails were included as an aged tissue that had never been regenerated.
source: The tails were included as an aged tissue that had never been regenerated.
evidence: This explains the rationale for sampling the tail.

claim: 30 samples were prepared for RNA sequencing and transcriptomic analysis.
source: In total, 30 samples were prepared for RNA sequencing and transcriptomic analysis.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: Trinity 20140413p1 was used for de novo assembly of the transcriptome.
source: Trinity 20140413p1 was used for this project, and we used multi-step in silico normalization for the sequencing reads (Grabherr et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics methods used.

claim: The final assembly result gave an N50 of 430, and the average contig length was 409.
source: The final assembly result gave an N50 of 430, and the average contig length was 409.
evidence: This describes the assembly quality metrics.

claim: All assembly work was performed on PSC Blacklight which is an SGI UV 1000cc-NUMA shared-memory system comprising 256 blades.
source: All assembly work was performed on PSC (Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center) Blacklight which is an SGI UV 1000cc-NUMA shared-memory system comprising 256 blades.
evidence: This describes the computational infrastructure used.

claim: The 16 cores on each blade share 128Gb of local memory.
source: The 16 cores on each blade share 128Gb of local memory.
evidence: This describes the computational infrastructure specifications.

claim: Bowtie 2 was used to align the original reads to the Trinity transcripts to obtain abundance estimates.
source: After assembly, the original reads (not in silico normalized) were aligned to the Trinity transcripts to obtain abundance estimates using Bowtie 2 (Langmead and Salzberg, 2012).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics methods used.

claim: RSEM software was used to estimate the expression levels based on the resulting alignments.
source: Then, RSEM software was used to estimate the expression levels based on the resulting alignments.
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics methods used.

claim: The edgeR Bioconductor package was used to identify differentially expressed transcripts.
source: After estimating abundance, we obtained the expression profiles for each sample, and the edgeR Bioconductor package was used to identify differentially expressed transcripts (Robinson et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes the bioinformatics methods used.

claim: The de novo assembled transcriptome was annotated against the human reference proteome using NCBI BLASTx.
source: The de novo assembled transcriptome was annotated against the human reference proteome (e-value<1E-10) using NCBI BLASTx (Altschul et al., 1990; Looso et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the annotation methods used.

claim: The UniProt IDs of the differentially regulated gene groups were used as 'gene lists' in the DAVID 6.7 online functional annotation tool for GO enrichment.
source: For GO enrichment, the UniProt IDs of the differentially regulated gene groups were used as 'gene lists' in the DAVID 6.7 online functional annotation tool (Huang et al., 2008, 2009).
evidence: This describes the GO enrichment methods used.

claim: The newt reference proteome was used as the source of background genes for GO enrichment analysis.
source: We used the newt reference proteome as the source of background genes.
evidence: This describes the GO enrichment methods used.

claim: GO terms with FDR<0.05 were considered enriched.
source: GO terms with FDR<0.05 were considered enriched.
evidence: This describes the statistical threshold used for GO enrichment.

claim: Linear regression analysis was performed with SigmaPlot 11.0 and Excel.
source: Linear regression analysis appearing in Figure 5A was performed with SigmaPlot 11.0 and Excel.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis methods used.

claim: Raw sequencing reads have been deposited in the NCBI's Sequence Read Archive database (BioProject accession: PRJNA288378).
source: Raw sequencing reads has been deposited in the NCBI's Sequence Read Archive (SRA) database (BioProject accession: PRJNA288378).
evidence: This describes the data availability.
